metadata.description: LMC660AIN quad op-amp (3 buffers + spare) · LMC660AIN
Audio is passive from the instrument jack to the first loop return; buffered thereafter
Nothing upstream of a loop return is ever buffered; fuzz lives first in Loop A
Fixed at three unity buffers regardless of lane count
Drives the A→B hop and downstream when A is active
Drives the chain output whenever B is last
Covers the all-loops-off state; one stage feeds every TO port
FX chain source is always low-Z (device FX send or return buffer); a buffer there is redundant
Shared divider biasing all buffers on a single 9 V rail
Non-inverting buffer topology, 1 MΩ input bias
1 MΩ bleeds on every switched node; AC coupling at buffer boundaries
LMC660-class CMOS output swing; TL074 only with caveat; 5.5 V-max parts excluded
1 µF film in/out of every buffer keeps DC off relay contacts
Each position cycles Off → A → B → A→B → Off independently
Applied Pre-TO = requested minus loops held by Pre-FX (A2P = Y1 and not X1)
One physical send/return pair per loop; a loop cannot sit at both positions at once
LEDs show applied routing; Pre-TO may display Off while its request is overridden
Loop A always precedes Loop B in series — wired contact order, not logic
Lane changes never bridge two paths; inherent to relay switching
Unselected lane tips float; only the selected lane connects
Complete state × relay × LED acceptance reference
DPDT per loop-at-position: COM in, NO to loop/buffer, NC bridge = bypass
Both relays of a loop tie NO contacts to the same jacks; interlock prevents double drive
Power loss or firmware fault → passive straight-through, loops bypassed, other lanes isolated
Output buffer relay-bypassed; de-energized = hardwire — keeps fail-safe honest with an active output
100 kΩ base pull-downs hold every coil off while MCU pins float at boot/ISP
Firmware hang → reset → boot state → hardwire; no relay held mid-state
Relay de-energized state is always the bypass/straight path
On power loss the loop relays remove the loops and their return buffers from circuit
Microcontroller replaces Revision A CMOS: debounce, states, allocation, drivers
One clean event per press; contact quality noncritical
Applied state computed before any relay/LED write — interlock cannot glitch
Strap at boot walks all 16 states — QC mode for made-to-order units
Three LEDs share MOSI/MISO/SCK; LED loads are programmer-safe
Spare UART/I²C reserved; must never compromise fail-safe requirements
Fourth amplifier parked as follower; future always-on tuner feed
Firmware and buffers lane-agnostic; lanes add relays and jacks only
Units built to order; capped runs; per-order config and self-test
1–4 standard; studios can order specific counts up to 8 in rack format
1590-class floor unit, 9 V pedal supply, suits 1–4 lanes
Internal linear supply, ±15 V audio rails, 2–8 lanes
Momentary NO on TS jacks: tip = switch node, sleeve = ground; no proprietary connectors
Empty jack reads pull-up = released; a missing switch can never read as stuck
Front normalled jacks for IN, loops, and footswitch inputs — never a parallel Y
Netlist-verified passive/no-firmware predecessor; truth-table and contact-matrix source
SingleLane.kicad_sch: netlist diffed pin-for-pin, ERC zero violations
One-loop buffered prototype that established debounce/driver pattern
Exported KiCad netlist diffed pin-by-pin against expected pin→net tables
Schematic accepted only with zero ERC violations
Continuity → rails → buffers → MCU walk; audio last
Unpowered continuity, state walk, interlock rows, power-loss test before gear connects
Worst case 3 coils + LEDs + logic + op-amp on a ≥100 mA isolated supply
Interlock caps active loops at 2; + K5 = 3 energized coils worst case
Standard pedal supply convention; center = GND, sleeve = +9 V raw
1N5817 series protection feeding coils and op-amp
Rack format runs bipolar linear supply; headroom non-issue
